name: Queen's Gambit
description: 1.d4 d5 2.c4: offer a wing pawn to win the centre.

lines.name: Exchange (4.cxd5)

notes.2: c4 attacks d5; if Black takes, White wins it back and owns the centre.
notes.6: cxd5 fixes Black's pawns and gives White a clear plan.
notes.8: Bg5 pins the f6 knight, the main defender of d5.
notes.10: e3 supports d4 and frees the f1 bishop.
notes.12: Bd3 develops towards Black's king and stops …Bf5.

lines.summary: Trade on d5, pin with Bg5, then e3 and Bd3: a clear plan for White.

lines.name: Exchange: 7…c6

notes.2: c4 attacks d5; if Black takes, White wins it back and owns the centre.
notes.6: cxd5 fixes Black's pawns and gives White a clear plan.
notes.8: Bg5 pins the f6 knight, the main defender of d5.
notes.10: e3 supports d4 and frees the f1 bishop.
notes.12: Bd3 develops towards Black's king and stops …Bf5.
notes.14: Qc2 stops …Bf5, which would trade Black's problem bishop.

lines.summary: Against …c6, Qc2 stops …Bf5; then Nf3 (or Nge2), castle and start the minority attack.

lines.name: Exchange: 7…h6

notes.2: c4 attacks d5; if Black takes, White wins it back and owns the centre.
notes.6: cxd5 fixes Black's pawns and gives White a clear plan.
notes.8: Bg5 pins the f6 knight, the main defender of d5.
notes.10: e3 supports d4 and frees the f1 bishop.
notes.12: Bd3 develops towards Black's king and stops …Bf5.
notes.14: Bh4 keeps the pin on the f6 knight.
notes.16: Qc2 stops …Bf5 and lines up on h7.

lines.summary: Against …h6, keep the pin with Bh4, then Qc2 as usual.

lines.name: Exchange: 5…c6

notes.2: c4 attacks d5; if Black takes, White wins it back and owns the centre.
notes.6: cxd5 fixes Black's pawns and gives White a clear plan.
notes.8: Bg5 pins the f6 knight, the main defender of d5.
notes.14: Qc2 stops …Bf5, which would trade Black's problem bishop.

lines.summary: Trade on d5, pin with Bg5, then Bd3 and Qc2 to keep Black's light-squared bishop passive.

lines.name: Exchange, minority attack

notes.2: c4 attacks d5; if Black takes, White wins it back and owns the centre.
notes.6: cxd5 fixes Black's pawns and gives White a clear plan.
notes.8: Bg5 pins the f6 knight, the main defender of d5.
notes.14: Qc2 stops …Bf5, which would trade Black's problem bishop.
notes.18: O-O completes development; now the queenside plan starts.
notes.20: Rab1 prepares b4-b5, the minority attack against Black's c6 pawn.

lines.summary: The minority attack: Rab1, b4, b5, and trade on c6 to leave Black a weak pawn.

lines.name: 4…Nxd5

notes.2: c4 attacks d5; if Black takes, White wins it back and owns the centre.
notes.6: cxd5 fixes Black's pawns and gives White a clear plan.
notes.8: e4 grabs the centre with tempo on the d5 knight.
notes.10: bxc3 gives White a big pawn centre.

lines.summary: If Black takes back with the knight, push e4 at once and build a big centre.

lines.name: Accepted (2…dxc4)

notes.2: c4 attacks d5; if Black takes, White wins it back and owns the centre.
notes.8: Bxc4 wins the pawn back with a lead in development.
notes.12: a4 stops …b5, which would gain space with tempo on the bishop.

lines.summary: Don't rush to win the pawn back: develop, retake on c4, and stop …b5 with a4.

lines.name: 7.a4 Nc6

notes.2: c4 attacks d5; if Black takes, White wins it back and owns the centre.
notes.8: Bxc4 wins the pawn back with a lead in development.
notes.12: a4 stops …b5, which would gain space with tempo on the bishop.
notes.14: Qe2 connects the rooks and supports a later d5 push.
notes.16: Rd1 puts the rook opposite the d4 pawn before taking it back.
notes.18: exd4 leaves White an isolated d-pawn, but with active pieces and d5 ideas.

lines.summary: White gets an isolated d-pawn with active pieces: aim for the d5 push.

lines.name: 5…Be7

notes.2: c4 attacks d5; if Black takes, White wins it back and owns the centre.
notes.8: Bxc4 wins the pawn back with a lead in development.
notes.10: O-O: develop quickly; Nc3, Qe2 and e4 come next.

lines.summary: Against the quiet …Be7, just castle and develop; aim for e4.

lines.name: Exchange (3.cxd5)

notes.2: c4 attacks d5; if Black takes, White wins it back and owns the centre.
notes.4: cxd5 makes a symmetrical structure where White keeps the extra move.
notes.14: Bb5 pins the c6 knight, adding pressure on Black's centre.

lines.summary: Against the Slav, trade on d5, develop fast and use the extra move: Bf4, e3, Nf3, Bb5.

lines.name: Exchange: 6…a6

notes.2: c4 attacks d5; if Black takes, White wins it back and owns the centre.
notes.4: cxd5 makes a symmetrical structure where White keeps the extra move.

lines.summary: Against …a6, develop the bishop to d3 first so …Bf5 is no longer possible.

lines.name: 2…Nf6

notes.2: c4 attacks d5; if Black takes, White wins it back and owns the centre.
notes.4: cxd5 wins space: Black can't keep a pawn on d5.
notes.6: Nf3 develops; e4 next builds a big centre.

lines.summary: Against 2…Nf6, take on d5 and develop; Black has given up the centre.

lines.name: Albin Countergambit (2…e5)

notes.2: c4 attacks d5; if Black takes, White wins it back and owns the centre.
notes.4: dxe5 takes the pawn; the d4 pawn will be a target later.
notes.6: Nf3 defends e5 and avoids the trap after 4.e3? Bb4+.
notes.8: g3 prepares Bg2, aiming the bishop at the queenside.
notes.10: Bg2 develops and eyes b7; the d4 pawn will need a lot of defending.

6.e3: …Bb4+ and …dxe3: the Lasker Trap, ending in …fxg1=N+!

lines.summary: Take the Albin pawn, develop with Nf3, g3 and Bg2, and keep the e5 pawn protected.
